newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain in selective trade, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain in selective trade, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 0.68 percent in range-bound and selective trade on Friday in reaction to Thursday's 2.02 percent drop, but volume was low, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed up 560.73 points at 82,566.84, after moving between 81,888 and 83,303. It gained 0.18 percent over the three-day week after 0.83 percent last week.
Trade volume dived to 16.93 trillion lira ($175.6 million), including a 2.02 trillion lira ($21 million) block deal on the wholesale market, from Thursday's 19.02 trillion ($198 million).

"The index remained squeezed betweeen 81,000-84,000. The rapid rise seen in the past two months has slowed down which shows the market is losing strength. I think the market has reached saturation," said Seyfullah Esen from Oki securities.
"There are no driving expecations left. But a downtrend is not awaited unless the index falls below 81,000. It it does, it may target 75,000," he said.
The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to an all-time high close of 83,772.33 on October 23, the tenth record in an uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level.
